stories.headline: Google DeepMind releases Gemini 4 Hydrogen with multi-model Orchestrator integration
stories.dek: Gemini 4 Hydrogen offers four thinking levels, a 1 million-token context window, and dynamic session switching via Google Antigravity.
detail: Google DeepMind has introduced Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a model optimized for execution speed, daily coding, and agentic workflows. Priced flat at $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens across its 1 million-token context window, the model achieves a score of 51 at its default high thinking level and 54 at its highest xhigh setting on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, outperforming Argon. It features four selectable thinking levels—low, medium, high, and xhigh—to align quality, latency, and token cost with task requirements.

Google also introduced Orchestrator in Google Antigravity, which dynamically switches between frontier models like Carbon and execution models like Hydrogen within a single session. On Terminal-Bench 4.0, Orchestrator achieved near-Carbon success rates while consuming 24% less quota and operating 19% faster on average. In multi-agent configurations, Carbon serves as a coordinator while Hydrogen powers worker and verifier agents to build and test code across isolated workspaces.

Compared to Gemini 3.8 Flash, Hydrogen finishes tasks 2.5 times faster at default high thinking and more than triples Terminal-Bench 4.1 scores from 18.2% to 57%, while reducing fabricated claims by more than five times. It ranks fifth overall on Agent Arena, scores 58.8% on HLE-Diamond, 52.3% on Vals Tax Agent Bench, 55.8% on Vals Legal Research Bench, 53.4% on the Multimodal Knowledge Agent benchmark, and 71.6% on Agents' Last Exam v1.1.
stories.why: Gemini 4 Hydrogen's low execution pricing and Orchestrator integration offer Rishi an efficient option for running fast evaluation and code-generation passes.

stories.headline: AWS releases SGLang-Neuron for model serving on Trainium accelerators
stories.dek: SGLang-Neuron connects the SGLang serving interface to AWS Trainium using an out-of-tree PyTorch plugin design.
detail: Amazon, in collaboration with RadixArk and Annapurna Labs, has released SGLang-Neuron through a public AWS Deep Learning Container. The tool connects the SGLang inference framework directly to AWS Trainium silicon via an out-of-tree plugin. The plugin architecture allows SGLang core to handle API serving, request lifecycles, RadixAttention, and prefix caching, while the plugin handles Trainium-specific model implementations, attention mechanisms, mixture-of-experts logic, and execution graph management.

The underlying execution uses TorchNeuron to register Trainium as a native PyTorch device. Custom kernels written with the Neuron Kernel Interface are integrated into the PyTorch operation path and compiled into executables using torch.compile. SGLang-Neuron also supports prefill-decode disaggregation, allowing a prefill server to compute the prompt KV cache and transfer it over Elastic Fabric Adapter via NIXL to a dedicated decode server for token generation.

Developers can launch the container using a public Amazon ECR image and serve models such as openai/gpt-oss-120b across eight tensor parallel and eight expert parallel ranks. The setup uses standard SGLang server flags to configure static memory fractions, context lengths up to 10,240 tokens, and chunked prefill settings.
stories.why: SGLang-Neuron provides Rishi with a practical framework for deploying large open models on non-NVIDIA cloud hardware using standard PyTorch workflows.

stories.headline: llama.cpp reaches version 1.0.0 with formal API stability guarantees
stories.dek: The project establishes semantic versioning rules for local LLM inference across more than 150 supported model architectures.
detail: The maintainers of llama.cpp and ggml have officially released libraries version 1.0.0, establishing a stable API and ABI contract for downstream software dependencies. Moving forward, both ggml-org projects will adhere strictly to semantic versioning rules, indicating breaking interface or binary incompatibilities through major-version increment bumps.

Over its three-and-a-half-year development history, llama.cpp has expanded to support over 150 machine learning architecture variants alongside mainstream speculative decoding methods. Its execution engine, ggml, uses dynamic libraries compiled for specific hardware backends to run multimodal models on consumer-grade local machines and enterprise servers.

To support the release, Hugging Face provided infrastructure tools including HF Buckets and HF Jobs to scale continuous integration testing. The project also expanded its network of self-hosted runners using dedicated hardware from NVIDIA, AMD, Qualcomm, Arm, IBM, and Intel to verify code changes prior to merging into master branches.
stories.why: The version 1.0.0 release provides Rishi with a stable, standardized local engine for running open-weight models without risk of sudden API breakage.

stories.headline: DeepSeek launches V4.1-Flash model with integrated tool APIs and dual billing
stories.dek: DeepSeek introduces five server-side built-in tools for deepseek-flash and unifies pricing across its Tool API platform.
detail: DeepSeek has released its new deepseek-flash model, designated as V4.1-Flash, featuring five built-in server-side execution tools across its Messages, Responses, and Chat Completions APIs. The server-side toolsuite includes Web Search, Deep Thinking Search for multi-step reasoning, File Input for inspecting PDFs, Office documents, and images, URL Reading, and mandatory Safety Checks for public apps.

The API relies on a dual-billing system, charging a separate tool usage fee in addition to token-based consumption. DeepSeek has formally unified its Tool API pricing structure for standalone services including Search, Fetch, OCR, Automatic Speech Recognition, and Text-to-Speech, with a temporary 50% discount currently applied to audio APIs.

By executing file parsing, web search, link retrieval, and moderation on the server side via flags such as deepseek_web_search, the framework removes the need for developers to maintain custom parsing pipelines or external search scrapers in client applications.
stories.why: Built-in server-side tool execution in DeepSeek V4.1-Flash allows Rishi to test document parsing and web search workflows without writing external scrapers.

stories.headline: OpenFold3 structure prediction model arrives on Amazon SageMaker JumpStart
stories.dek: Columbia University and the OpenFold Consortium deploy their Apache 2.0 all-atom biomolecular model to managed cloud endpoints.
detail: The OpenFold Consortium and Columbia University's AlQuraishi Lab have made OpenFold3-preview available on Amazon SageMaker JumpStart under an open-source Apache 2.0 license. The all-atom biomolecular prediction model generates joint 3D structures for single protein chains, multi-chain protein complexes, protein-nucleic acid assemblies, and protein-ligand binding complexes directly from sequence inputs and SMILES representations.

Because biomolecular folding calculations scale with sequence length and can require several minutes per request, OpenFold3 deploys to SageMaker Asynchronous Inference endpoints rather than real-time endpoints capped at 60 seconds. Users submit requests to Amazon S3 and invoke asynchronous endpoints, which queue jobs with execution timeouts up to one hour and write structural predictions and confidence scores back to S3.

The managed endpoints run inside AWS-maintained containers on GPU instances such as ml.g6.4xlarge and ml.g6.12xlarge with network isolation. The setup includes automatic request queuing and the ability to scale endpoint instances to zero during idle periods to reduce overall infrastructure costs.
stories.why: OpenFold3 serves as an accessible architectural reference for Rishi on how to package complex, multi-minute deep learning inference pipelines on cloud GPUs.

stories.headline: Where was Nvidia’s security team?
stories.dek: Nvidia’s security chief quietly left in August, and now that CEO Jensen Huang has stepped down over his relationships, including one with an executive at a company suspected of funneling chips to China, a former intellig
detail: Outsiders had little reason to notice when Nvidia’s longtime chief security officer and head of product security stepped down in August. Just two and a half months later, CEO Jensen Huang himself left the company over growing questions about his extramarital relationships — starting with an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore data center company that U.S. investigators suspect of funneling Nvidia chips to China, then widening to reports about two separate affairs with Nvidia employees.

At the time, David Reber, who spent four years as CSO and seven at Nvidia overall, said he was leaving for health reasons. “This wasn’t a pivot I had planned. But I know what needs to come first: family and health,” he wrote on LinkedIn in late August, disclosing that he’d been diagnosed with young-onset Parkinson’s more than two years ago.

Reber’s replacement, Saša Zdjelar, previously spent 17 years at ExxonMobil in Houston, leaving as a senior IT manager before spending one year at Salesforce and several years at the cybersecurity company ReversingLabs. Zdjelar didn’t respond to questions Thursday about the transition or what the security team knew.

Nothing public connects Reber’s or Zdjelar’s role changes to the Megaspeed matter, but it seems fair to wonder what Nvidia’s security team knew about the government’s scrutiny of Megaspeed and about Huang’s relationships, and whether anyone raised concerns. Reber didn’t respond to questions Thursday. Nvidia also has not answered our related questions.

stories.headline: GitHub introduces standard SKILL.md specification for reusable AI agent workflows
stories.dek: A structured file directory format enables developers to share versioned instructions and operational rules across multiple agent platforms.
detail: GitHub has published a guide on agent skills, a methodology for packaging repeatable developer context into versioned directories centered around a SKILL.md specification. The file format defines specific triggers, inputs, and operational boundaries for task execution, allowing team instructions to be shared across platforms like Claude Code, Cursor, and GitHub Copilot without duplicating context.

The specification separates instructions from environmental permissions, requiring host applications to supply database credentials, tool access, and API keys. To ensure portability, project-specific variables such as table schemas or environment parameters are isolated into a resolved manifest file created by initialization skills, separating repository details from team formatting rules.

The workflow pattern emphasizes isolated verification roles and human approval gates across pipeline stages. For example, the Proof Agent uses a dedicated verifier skill that evaluates diffs and outputs evidence-backed PASS, FAIL, or PARTIAL statuses without taking guidance from the primary coding agent's self-assessment.
stories.why: Adopting the SKILL.md specification offers Rishi a clean, modular structure for defining reproducible execution steps in his agentic vision and data pipelines.

india.headline: Jensen Huang’s Exit: How Deep Does NVIDIA’s AI Ecosystem Run In India?
india.dek: Jensen Huang’s exit from NVIDIA has put the spotlight on the company’s leadership and succession plans. But for India, the…
detail: NVIDIA’s influence in India extends far beyond GPU sales, spanning AI infrastructure, software, developer ecosystems, startup incubation and direct equity investments.

With Indian data centre operators committing billions of dollars to NVIDIA-powered infrastructure, and enterprises and startups building on its CUDA-led software stack, the company has become deeply embedded in the country's AI ambitions.

As Jensen Huang exits, the bigger question is whether India can reduce its dependence on a single technology provider, particularly as geopolitical uncertainties, export restrictions and competing chip architectures reshape access to AI compute.

Jensen Huang’s exit from NVIDIA has put the spotlight on the company’s leadership and succession plans. But for India, the more consequential question is what happens to an ecosystem that has increasingly come to depend on the American chipmaker for its AI ambitions.
